why: Level-order BFS with a twist: process the queue one level at a time and keep the last node of each level. (A DFS that visits right before left and records the first node at each new depth also works.)
hints: Which node is visible from the right at depth d? Think about all nodes at that depth in left-to-right order.
BFS level by level: at the start of a round the queue holds exactly one level; the last node you pop in that round is the visible one.
Loop: n = len(queue); pop n nodes, pushing left then right children; append the value of the n-th popped node. O(n) time, O(width) space.
pitfalls: The visible node is not always a right child: in [1,2,3,4] the deepest visible node is 4, a left child.
Fix the level size before popping, or children added during the round get mixed into the current level.
